proposals.before: When he came of age he was a wastrel who shunned honest work and lived by smuggling salt and raiding as a outlaw.
proposals.after: When he came of age he was a wastrel who shunned honest work and lived by smuggling salt and raiding as an outlaw.
proposals.reason: English article error: 'as a outlaw' should be 'as an outlaw'.

proposals.before: In his early years, Qi let his sons and others go out with Qian Liu, and from time to time helped him out when he was short of means.
proposals.after: Qi then began to let his sons and others associate with Qian Liu, and from time to time helped him out when he was short of means.
proposals.reason: 起始 here is Zhong Qi (起) plus 始 'then began', after the physiognomist departed—not 'in his early years'.

proposals.before: In the second year of the Qianfu era (875), Wang Ying, a deputy general in Zhexi, rose in rebellion. Dong Chang, military commissioner at Shijian, recruited local militia to suppress the rebels, had Qian Liu appointed deputy commander, attacked Wang Ying, and defeated him.
proposals.after: In the second year of the Qianfu era (875), Wang Ying, a deputy general in Zhexi, rose in rebellion. Dong Chang, garrison commander at Shijian, recruited local militia to suppress the rebels, had Qian Liu appointed deputy commander, attacked Wang Ying, and defeated him.
proposals.reason: 石鑒鎮將 is a garrison commander (鎮將), not a military commissioner (節度使).

proposals.before: That year Bi Shiduo imprisoned Gao Piao, throwing Huainan into chaos. Xu Yue, military commissioner at Liuhe, captured Suzhou.
proposals.after: That year Bi Shiduo imprisoned Gao Piao, throwing Huainan into chaos. Xu Yue, garrison commander at Liuhe, captured Suzhou.
proposals.reason: 六合鎮將 is a garrison commander (鎮將), not a military commissioner (節度使).

proposals.before: Emperor Zhaozong had Grand Councilor Wang Pu take charge of Yuezhou. Pu petitioned that the territory be transferred to Liu, and the Weisheng command was redesignated Zhendong. Qian Liu was made Military Commissioner of both Zhenhai and Zhendong, elevated to Acting Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat, and granted an iron tally forgiving nine capital crimes.
proposals.after: Emperor Zhaozong had Grand Councilor Wang Pu take charge of Yuezhou. Pu petitioned that the territory be transferred to Liu, and the Weisheng command was redesignated Zhendong. Qian Liu was made Military Commissioner of both Zhenhai and Zhendong, elevated to Acting Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat, and granted an iron tally forgiving nine capital crimes.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Guardian (太保).

proposals.before: Emperor Zhaozong sent Grand Councilor Wang Pu to govern Yuezhou; Pu requested that it be granted to Liu, whereupon Weisheng Army was changed to Zhendong Army, Liu was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, given the additional posts of Acting Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat, and granted an iron tally forgiving nine deaths.
proposals.after: Emperor Zhaozong sent Grand Councilor Wang Pu to govern Yuezhou; Pu requested that it be granted to Liu, whereupon Weisheng Army was changed to Zhendong Army, Liu was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, given the additional posts of Acting Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat, and granted an iron tally forgiving nine deaths.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Guardian (太保).

proposals.before: In the third year he was further promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: In the third year he was further promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 守太保 is Acting Grand Guardian (太保), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: In the third year, he was further promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: In the third year, he was further promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.

proposals.before: Wu-Yue had held its realm since late Tang, while Yang Xingmi and Li Ju controlled the Jiang-Huai.
proposals.after: Wu-Yue had held its realm since late Tang, while Yang Xingmi and the Li occupied the Jiang-Huai.
proposals.reason: 李據有江淮 uses 據 'occupy' as a verb, not a personal name Li Ju.

proposals.before: Chu's chancellor Wu Cheng hurriedly mobilized and marched out; Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Dezhao held that the imperial army surely had not yet crossed the Huai, and disputed with Cheng before Chu—he could not be overborne.
proposals.after: Chu's chancellor Wu Cheng hurriedly mobilized and marched out; Chancellor Yuan Dezhao held that the imperial army surely had not yet crossed the Huai, and disputed with Cheng before Chu—he could not be overborne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 相國元德昭 is chancellor (相國), not Vice Censor-in-Chief.

decisions.reason: The indefinite article before outlaw must be 'an'.
起 is Zhong Qi, the preceding person's name, while 始 means that he then began allowing the association; it does not mean 'in his early years.'
鎮將 is a garrison commander, not the higher office of military commissioner denoted by 節度使.
六合鎮將 identifies Xu Yue as Liuhe's garrison commander, not a military commissioner.
檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant; Grand Guardian would be 太保.
The literal field repeats the same mistranslation of 檢校太尉 as Acting Grand Guardian.
守太保 is Acting Grand Guardian; Grand Preceptor would be 太師.
The literal field repeats the same mistranslation of 太保 as Grand Preceptor.

decisions.after: Wu-Yue had held its realm since late Tang, while Yang Xingmi and the Li family held the Jiang-Huai region.
decisions.reason: In 楊行密、李據有江淮, 據 is the verb 'held' or 'occupied,' not part of a personal name Li Ju. 'The Li family' gives the dynastic reference idiomatic English form.
相國 explicitly identifies Yuan Dezhao as chancellor, not Vice Censor-in-Chief.
